evidence.name: sharp_polynomial_presieve.md
evidence.text:
# A polynomial input presieve for the unaltered signed FM outside coefficient

Set L=log x, U=V=x^.24 and D=x^.49. Keep every prime label, strict threshold and squarefree condition in the native signed large-product coefficient B(k), with k=n−2. For h≥2 write

    C_h(f) = Σ_{x/2<n≤x} f_x(n) 1_{P⁻(k)>h} μ²(k) B(k).

The bounded output f may be the native Φ, ψ, Φ−ψ, or their positive or negative parts. For large x it has bounded rank and P⁻(n)>x^ζ on its support, ζ=1/(4·10^11), and ∑|f|≪_f x/L. Its signed and unsigned profiles satisfy the primitive product progression estimate proved in uniform_native_transfer.md, including common upper endpoints. All normalized sums use S_b∼S₂x/(2L).

**Theorem.** Fix 0<a<1 and w=exp(L^a). Then

    lim_{ε↓0} limsup_{x→∞} |C_w(f)−C_{x^ε}(f)|/S_b = 0.

In particular, for any requested error one can keep only squarefree physical inputs with every prime above one fixed power of x and with rank at most ⌊1/ε⌋. This is collective cancellation over the actual sharp tagged sum, including all original owners. It makes no statement about the sum of absolute row weights or an independently selected tag mask. The small-power exponent is chosen before letting x grow.

## Sieve cost with a fixed polynomial threshold

Write z=x^ε with fixed 0<ε<ζ. Apply the exact Vaughan identity used in uniform_native_transfer.md with the same original U,V,D. Prime inputs have weight θ(k) in either presieve. The proper powers and rough nonsquarefree inputs are negligible after the absolute divisor bound, since repeated primes now exceed z. It suffices to evaluate the same two Type I terms and the short product. Their moduli e₀≤x^.49 have no prime ≤z. The primitive progression is n≡2 mod e₀. Coefficients with the common factors log k extracted by partial summation are bounded by O(L) after grouping. For the short and Λ convolution sums this follows from Σ_{j|e₀}Λ(j)=log e₀. The positivity comparison can use the sum of the absolute ungrouped coefficients with the same O(L) bound.

For each e₀ sieve k/e₀ by the odd primes up to z, using the two dimension-one fundamental-lemma weights λ^± of level x^.002. They bracket the integer presieve pointwise. For each sign of the profile and coefficient, the total progression errors follow from the profile progression bound at level x^.492. In fact the representation e₀d is unique because primes of d are ≤z and primes of e₀ exceed z. The maximum cumulative coefficient is O(L), and the common weight log k costs one partial summation. All active n are coprime to d, so the sole remaining primitive exclusion is (n,e₀)=1. The main sum of λ^±(d)/φ(d) is g_z(1+O(E_s)) uniformly, where g_z=∏_{2<p≤z}(1−1/(p−1)), s=.002/ε, E_s≪s^(−s/2) as s→∞ with an absolute dimension-one constant. The dimension follows from the Mertens product for 1/(p−1) away from 2. The same upper and lower weights handle positive and negative coefficients.

On rough moduli, Σ_{e₀≤x^.49} R_z(e₀)/φ(e₀) ≪ 1/ε. This follows by comparing the Euler product, including all prime powers, to ∏_{z<p≤x}(1−1/p)⁻¹ with a bounded convergent correction. Also g_z L≪1/ε. Summing the majorant cost, including ∑|f|≪_f S_b, pays O_f(ε⁻² E_s) S_b+o_{ε,f}(S_b). This fixed-ε estimate is essential. A positive power of L multiplying E_s at fixed ε would invalidate the limiting argument.

## The degree-zero and degree-one Möbius means

For m odd put R_z(m)=1_{P⁻(m)>z}, with R_z(1)=1. At fixed ε and bounded 0≤v≤1, define the rough harmonic Möbius prefix A_z(x^v)=Σ_{m≤x^v}μ(m)R_z(m)/φ(m). Then, writing t=v/ε,

    A_z(x^v) = ρ(t) + o_ε(1),
    (log z)⁻¹ Σ_{m≤x^v} μ(m)R_z(m)log m/φ(m)
        = tρ(t)−∫₀ᵗρ(u)du + o_ε(1),

uniformly in v. Indeed m has bounded squarefree rank at fixed ε. Expand by rank j, divide the unordered labeled counts by j!, and use Mertens' theorem separately in each normalized logarithmic prime coordinate. The reciprocal p−1 may replace p with o(1) error, and repeated prime coordinates cost o(1). For j≥1 the cumulative limit of a rank j positive measure is continuous. Common-endpoint convergence is therefore uniform on the compact interval; the mass at the unit is handled exactly. The signed limit is the finite series

    Σ_{j≤t} (−1)^j/j! ∫_{u_i≥1,Σu_i≤t} du₁⋯duⱼ/(u₁⋯uⱼ).

It equals 1 on [0,1], and multiplication of its boundary derivative by t=Σu_i gives tρ′(t)=−ρ(t−1) for t>1. This specifies the Dickman function. Partial summation yields the second relation. Its standard properties give ∫₀^∞ρ(t)dt=e^γ and factorial decay. For the latter, tρ(t)=∫_{t−1}ᵗρ(t′)dt′ and monotonicity suffice. Exclusion of the at most 256 prime divisors of n or nℓ changes these prefixes by o_ε(1), with the same normalization in the log moment. The cost is O_ε(Σ_{p|nℓ}1/(p−1))=o_ε(1) where ℓ>z. For the second displayed prefix one multiplies this absolute bound by O(1/ε).

## The signed transfer

Mertens gives g_z log z→S₂e^(−γ), with S₂=2∏_{p>2}(1−1/(p−1)²). Put t₀=.24/ε. The first Type I principal per output is g_z[A_n(U)log k−B_n(U)], with B_n now the logarithmic harmonic prefix. Its difference from S₂ has limsup bounded by a constant times ε⁻¹ρ(t₀)+∫_{t₀}^∞ρ. For the Λ subtraction the main prefix has argument U, and the factor from summing log ℓ/φ(ℓ^j) costs O(L). The exact common-prime term has an extra 1/ℓ and is negligible, since all ℓ>z and the harmonic absolute prefix is O(1/ε). For the short-product subtraction the two main arguments D/ℓ and U are at least U whenever nonempty. The monotonicity of ρ and uniform convergence bound their difference by 2ρ(t₀)+o_ε(1). Its common-prime correction is negligible for the same reason. Thus all remaining principal errors divided by S_b are bounded in limsup by

    O_f( ε⁻¹ρ(.24/ε) + ∫_{.24/ε}^∞ρ + ε⁻²E_{.002/ε} ).

This expression tends to zero with ε. The original w transfer equals the same prime sum minus S₂Σf, with o(S_b) error. Subtraction proves the theorem.

**Scope in the closing ledger.** After choosing ε sufficiently small one may attempt the fixed-rank, jointly polynomially rough ORIGINAL k and k+2 problem, with prescribed tolerance on its entire sharp complement. The physical semiprimes and all associated positive and negative output terms still occur. A favorable source-specific estimate for the retained core is required for a strictly positive twin reserve. A restriction on k alone inserted into f cannot invoke its original product progression bound.

Koukoulopoulos, The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Theorem 19.1 (two-sided fundamental lemma): https://dms.umontreal.ca/~koukoulo/documents/publications/primes.pdf
Liu, Park and Song, Theorem 3.2 (underlying bounded-rank prime product progression estimate): https://doi.org/10.1007/s40993-017-0089-3
Lagarias, Euler's constant: Euler's work and modern developments, Theorem 3.5.1 (Dickman integral): https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X

evidence.name: SMALL_INPUT_COMPENSATION.md
evidence.text:
# Signed compensation of semiprime input and localization at two small prime factors

For fixed $0<c<1/400$ set $L=\log x$, $V=x^c$, $U=x^{c\tau}$ with a fixed smooth probability density supported in $1<\tau<2$, and $D=x^c$. The product cutoff is automatic on the retained rows. Write $F(y)=\mathbb P(U<y)$, $T=x^{2c}$, and $H=x^{1/2-3c}$. Retain $R_w(k)\mu^2(k)$, $k=n-2$, and the original physical window throughout. Denote the averaged complete coefficient by $B(k)$. The original sharp complete outside sum against $f=\Phi-\psi$ equals the sum against $B$ up to $o_c(x/L)$ under the fixed-profile calibration proved in the first packet: $UV\le x^{3c}$, the lower Euler range is $U\ge x^c$, and the short-product block is empty. Apply the same calibration separately to $f_+=\max(f,0)$ and $f_-=\max(-f,0)$, fixed bounded piecewise profiles on the same output support.

Define the smooth prefix $M(r)=\sum_{d\mid r}\mu(d)(1-F(d))$. On every squarefree composite $k$ the physical $\ell$-row for $\ell>V$ equals $b_\ell(k)=-(\log\ell)M(k/\ell)$. On prime $k$ the true row is zero because the unit boundary cancels it. Introduce the explicit correction
$$
 W(\ell,k)=1+F(\ell)\frac{\log(k/\ell)}{\log\ell},\qquad
 B'(k)=B(k)-\sum_{\ell\mid k,\ V<\ell\le H,\ \ell\text{ prime}} W(\ell,k)b_\ell(k).
$$
At large $x$ the low rows in the sum have composite input, since $k\ge x/2-2>H$.

**Low-row identity.** For any fixed bounded-profile test $g$ satisfying the physical primitive progression bounds (PC) both for $g$ and its absolute envelope as in the first packet,
$$
 \sum_{n\in I_x}R_w(k)\mu^2(k)g(n)
       \sum_{\ell\mid k,\ V<\ell\le H} W(\ell,k)b_\ell(k)=o_{c,a,g}(x/L),
$$
where the sum is over prime labels. The proof retains all divisors in the prefix, including the unit. Write
$$
 W(\ell,k)\log\ell=(1-F(\ell))\log\ell+F(\ell)\log k.
$$
Thus both parts have scalar $\ell$ coefficients, and the second uses a smooth physical prefix via partial summation. After writing the prefix as its integral of sharp cutoffs, the modulus is $\ell m\le Hx^{2c}=x^{1/2-c}$. The $w$-smooth Bonferroni factor multiplies this by $x^{o(1)}$, leaving level below $x^{1/2-c/2}$. Each folded modulus has $O_c(1)$ possibilities for the distinguished prime since $\ell>x^c$; its smaller-prime factors determine the presieve fold uniquely. Replacing squarefree inputs before this calculation costs $o_c(x/L)$ by the divisor moment proof in the first packet: $W\le1+1/c$ and the corresponding absolute coefficients are $O_c(\tau(k)L)$. The formula $m\mid k/\ell$ becomes $\ell m\mid k$ even allowing a shared prime. Its primitive main per $\ell$ uses
$$
 \frac{g_w}{\ell-1}
 [ A_{n\ell,w}(U)-\ell^{-1} A_{n\ell,w}(U/\ell)].
$$
The first term has arbitrary logarithmic cancellation uniformly in $\tau$ since $U\ge x^c$. The second has the factor $\ell^{-1}\le x^{-c}$. These conclusions persist after multiplying by the indicated $\ell$ coefficients and summing their harmonic weights. This proves the low-row identity solely at the complete signed level.

Accordingly the following full *signed* expression has the same total as the native outside sum up to $o_c(x/L)$:
$$
 \sum_{n\in I_x} R_w(k)\mu^2(k)
  [ f_+(n)B(k)-f_-(n)B'(k)].
$$
All original higher-rank companions and their new multipliers are included. The correction is applied only to the negative output channel.

**Physical sectors.** The contribution of the prime input itself is zero. On a distinct semiprime $k=pq$ with $p<q$, if $p\le V$ the raw and corrected totals are zero. If $V<p\le H$, the two raw rows are $-\log p$ and $-F(p)\log q$. Since $q>H$ for large $x$, the $W$-weighted low $p$-row equals their entire sum. Hence $B'=0$ and $B\le0$. If $p>H$ both primes lie in the band $[x^{1/2-3c},x^{1/2+3c}]$. Its absolute contribution is $O_{f,\zeta}((c+1/L)x/L)$ uniformly in $c$: for fixed $p$ upper-sieve $q$ and $pq+2$ as in the first packet and sum $\sigma(p)/p$ over that band. Here, in all cases, two primes both $\le H$ cannot produce an input $k\in(x/2-2,x]$, since $H^2=x^{1-6c}$.

If $k$ is squarefree composite with no prime factor $\le T$, all its row prefixes are 1, $B=-\log k$, and $B'=(j-1)\log k$, where $j$ counts all its primes $\le H$. At rank at least three, $j\ge1$ since three primes above $H$ cannot divide $k\le x$. Hence $f_+B-f_-B'\le0$ on this entire sector.

Suppose $k$ has exactly one prime factor $s\le T$ and at least one other factor. Every row for a prime exceeding $T$ has prefix $F(s)$, since its divisor subsets of size at most $T$ can only be $1,s$. If $s\le V$ no eligible small label exists and all rows vanish. If $V<s\le T$, the small owner's quotient has prefix 1. Consequently
$$
 B=-\log s-F(s)\log(k/s)\le0.
$$
Its $W$-weighted small row equals this expression. Each other low label $p>T$ adds $F(s)\log k$ to the corrected coefficient. Thus $B'\ge0$ and the total is nonpositive. When *all* factors of $k$ are $\le T$ and there is just one, $k$ is prime and was already covered.

If the nontrivial product of *all* the primes of $k$ at most $T$ is $\le V$, none of these small primes is an eligible label. For each large owner the prefix is the complete divisor Möbius sum of this nontrivial product, hence all rows vanish. This argument is exact, including the weak face at $V$.

**One-sided complete localization.** Define $\mathcal E_{c,\delta,K}$ to consist of squarefree $k$ with $3\le\omega(k)\le K$, $P^-(k)>x^\delta$, at least two distinct prime divisors at most $x^{2c}$, and the product of all its prime divisors at most $x^{2c}$ greater than $x^c$. For $0<\delta<c$, the whole outside source has the upper bound
$$
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal U_{\mathscr B^c}(x)
 &\le\sum_{\substack{n\in I_x\\k=n-2\in\mathcal E_{c,\delta,K}}}
 R_w(k)\mu^2(k)[f_+(n)B(k)-f_-(n)B'(k)]\\
 &\quad +O_{f,\zeta}(c x/L)
   +O_{c,f,\zeta,\mathrm{density}}((\delta+2^{-K})x/L)
   +o_{c,a,f}(x/L).
 \end{aligned}
$$
To trim the small-prime and large-rank tails, apply the smooth Fourier–Euler proof to every raw and corrected row before restricting: the prime owner is now $\ell>x^c$, so the two-form sieve can use $z=x^{\min(\zeta,c/100)}$; $W\le1+1/c$; and the uniformly smooth cutoff has scale $cL$. A prime $p\le x^\delta$ in $k$ must belong to the quotient because $\delta<c$. For $\omega(k)>K$, every owner's quotient has rank at least $K$. This proves the displayed error. Constants in the second error may grow as $c$ shrinks; choose $c$ first and then $\delta,K$. No uniform limit in all three variables is asserted. The first error has a constant independent of $c$ for every sufficiently large $x$ after fixing $c$.

Bound the last residual with its full original $f_+$ and $f_-$ and a fixed margin to prove the desired outside estimate, after paying the indicated errors. This paper reduction supplies no favorable bound for that residual and credits zero net terminal saving. In particular, the fact that its inputs have two small primes does not imply the residual is negligible: their allowed range and the signed coefficients both depend on $c$. The same statement holds for the balanced output triple sector alone by multiplying $f_\pm$ by its exact fixed-profile indicator.

Keep the fixed smooth law of $\tau$ on $(1,2)$ and the definitions of $B,B',F,f_\pm$ from the small-input compensation packet. In particular $\mathcal W$ denotes the sum of $f_+B-f_-B'$ against $R_w\mu^2$; prime-input coefficients are evaluated in the original owner formula and are zero.

## 1. Bounds at these cutoffs

The folded Type-I and low-label moduli after inserting at most $R=O(\log L)$ presieve primes are at most $HTw^R=x^{1/2-\eta+o(1)}$. Thus the same *fixed* progression level $1/2-\eta/2$ suffices. $$
 \mathcal U_{\mathscr B^c}=\mathcal W+o_{a,b,\eta,f}(x/L)
 =A(f)-\mathfrak S_2\sum_n f_x(n)+o_{a,b,\eta,f}(x/L).

## 2. Exact restoration on zero small factors

Put
$$
 g_T=\prod_{2<p\le T}(1-1/(p-1)),\qquad
 P_T=\sum_{T<p\le H}\frac1{p-1},\qquad
 J(k)=\#\{T<p\le H:p\mid k\}.
$$

$$
 B(k)=-(1-1_{k\ {\rm prime}})\log k,\qquad
 B'(k)=[J(k)-1+1_{k\ {\rm prime}}]\log k.
$$
A prime in the window has $J(k)=0$. Therefore
$$
 \mathcal W_0=A(f)-
 \sum_{n\in I_x} R_T(k)\mu^2(k)(\log k)
        [f_x(n)+J(k)f_{-,x}(n)].
$$
This identity keeps the true prime-input mass, including its sign on the negative output wall.

The two required remaining prime-free populations are elementary consequences of (PC):
$$
 \sum_n R_T(k)\mu^2(k)g(n)=g_T\sum_n g(n)+O_A(xL^{-A}),
$$
$$
 \sum_n R_T(k)\mu^2(k)J(k)g(n)
  =g_T P_T\sum_n g(n)+O_A(xL^{-A})
$$
for $g=f,f_-$ and their positive envelopes (the implied constants depend on $a,b,\eta,f,A$). To see this, use Bonferroni for odd primes through $T$ at truncation $C_A\log L$. Every output prime exceeds $T$ for large $x$. In the first principal all small coprime factors are thus present. In the second, mark one $p\in(T,H]$, so $q=p e$ has a unique split into its one large-prime factor and a $T$-smooth factor. Its level is $\le HT^{O(\log L)}<x^{1/2-\eta/2}$. Exclusions $p\mid n$ cost at most $O_f(x^{-\zeta})$ per output by its bounded rank. The elementary symmetric principal tail from small primes is bounded by a factorial tail with mean $O(\log L)$; the extra prime sum costs $O(\log L)$. Taking the Bonferroni truncation constant and the discrepancy accuracy large enough pays any fixed log power. For squareful $R_T$-rough inputs the population is $O(x/T)$; the test $J(k)$ is at most $O(L)$, so removing them is harmless.  \mathcal W_{\ge1}
 &=L g_T\bigg[\sum_n f_x(n)+P_T\sum_n f_{-,x}(n)\bigg]
                   -\mathfrak S_2\sum_n f_x(n)+o(S_b).
 \end{aligned}}
$$
The calibrated complete signed mass on *all* inputs with at least one small prime is therefore explicit. Recovering its favorable zero-small counterpart restores the still unknown $A(f)$. This is the arithmetic content of the representation.

## 3. Obstruction to using the small-factor residual alone

The exactly-one sector satisfies $\mathcal W_1\le0$ by the pointwise calculation. Thus $\mathcal W_{\ge2}\ge\mathcal W_{\ge1}$. By Mertens,
$$
 g_T\sim e^{-\gamma}\mathfrak S_2/\log T,\qquad
 P_T=(1-b)\log L+O(1).
$$
If $\Pi(f_-)=\lim (2L/x)\sum_n f_{-,x}(n)>0$, the main term in the preceding box has normalized size
$$
 \frac{\mathcal W_{\ge1}}{S_b}
 \sim \tfrac12 e^{-\gamma}(1-b)\Pi(f_-)\,L^{1-b}\log L .
$$
Only the leading asymptotic is asserted here. The exact $g_T,P_T$ formula above gives the stronger absolute $o(S_b)$ error. Positivity of the fixed-profile mean follows without the full historical computation: restrict the three distinct output primes to fixed disjoint logarithmic bands near $(.30,.33,.37)$ whose sum equals one, staying away from all nontrivial cuts. Each factor has coordinate in $(1/4,9/20)$; $H=1-3=-2$, the output is good, and its outside profile equals $-2$. PNT partial summation gives positive mass on such a small open ordered region. No claim about primality of the shift is needed.

Consequently the one-sided shortcut which discards the entire complement of the at-least-two-small-prime source has a divergent positive right-hand side, even though the full physical source is on scale $S_b$. A joint estimate retaining the negative zero-small mass is essential. This is a scoped obstruction to the subpower truncation under the verified signs. It assigns no fixed advantage to the original endpoint. For the *positive* part alone, the omitted zero-small composites also have normalized mass asymptotic to $\tfrac12 e^{-\gamma}\Pi(f_+)L^{1-b}$, provided $\Pi(f_+)>0$, with the prime exception contributing $O_f(S_b)$ by a two-linear-form upper sieve on the prime and its shifted rough output.

# Complete semiprime-input slab for the native outside source

Let $x/2<n\le x$, $k=n-2$, $L=\log x$, $\epsilon=10^{-9}$ and $S^\circ=\mathfrak S_2 x/(2L)$. Put $f=\Phi-\psi$ as in `REAL1B.FM.Direct.outsideProfile` at `43facedcf40b2f998aa47f7198d6b9b5feb5b792`. Let $E$ denote $k=pq$, both factors prime, $x^{.492}<p\le x^{.494}$. Both factors exceed $x^{.24}$, $p<q$, $k>x^{.49}$, and for every fixed $0<a<1$ the subpower input presieve is one eventually. The native owner coefficient is exactly $-\log k$. Define $U_E$ to be the contribution of these inputs and $P^-(n)>x^{.21}$. Define $U_{E,4}$ to include just the rank-four outputs within this same population. With $a_E=\log(31369/31119)$,

$$
0\le\limsup U_{E,4}/S^\circ < 2.3\cdot10^{-8},\qquad
0\le\limsup U_E/S^\circ \le (4/.504)a_E+(2.3\cdot10^{-8})/3 < .063504604 .
$$

This controls a true positive contribution to the outside upper bound. The remaining triples in this slab and the unsieved complement of the slab still enter the full calculation. $S^\circ\sim S_b$ by the independent shifted-prime normalization argument.

## Physical signs

A nonsquarefree output has zero weight. On a squarefree output with the stated roughness all prime coordinates $t_i=\log p_i/\log n$ exceed $.21$. There are at most four. For a composite assign $r_i=1$ to each coordinate at most $1/2+\epsilon$ and $r_i=2$ to a larger coordinate. The latter can occur at most once, exceeds $2(1/5-\epsilon)$, and every assigned coordinate has zero tiny cost. The witness sum is at most five. Thus every such composite is good. The box selector needs five factors, so $f=-\max(-H,0)$. The prime itself has zero native weight. A semiprime has at most the smaller singleton in $H$ and hence $H\ge0$. On three primes $H\ge 1-3=-2$ since pair coefficients are nonnegative and the full product exceeds the cutoff.

On four primes every singleton enters and all three-prime products exceed the cutoff. Each pair contributes precisely when $t_i+t_j\le1/2-2\epsilon$. Within each of the three complementary pair partitions exactly one pair contributes unless its sums have distance strictly less than $2\epsilon$ from $1/2$. In that case neither contributes. Hence $-f$ equals the number of these exceptional partitions. Each is counted twice by the semiprime divisors on its two sides. Its largest value is three. On the whole slab the pointwise cost is at most two times the rough-output weight plus one third of the rank-four cost.

## Distribution for the specific input primes

Elementary prime partial summation gives the mass of the unweighted $E$ in the interval as $(a_E+o(1))x/(2L)$, using $a_E=\int_{.492}^{.494}dt/[t(1-t)]$. The logarithmic weight on every row may be bounded above by $L$.

For divisor moduli $h$, the relevant residue is $k=-2\pmod h$. In dyadic product rectangles, $X_0=MN\asymp x$ and the longer prime factor has $\log N/\log X_0\in[.506-o(1),.508+o(1)]$. Fouvry–Radziwiłł Theorem 1.1 supplies an absolute mean of the primitive discrepancy in the range $N^{56/23}X_0^{-17/23+\eta}\le Q\le NX_0^{-\eta}$. Since $(56\cdot .508-17)/23<.498$ and $.504<.506$, every dyadic block between $x^{.499}$ and $x^{.504}$ is covered with a fixed margin. The two prime coefficients are bounded by one. The longer one satisfies Siegel–Walfisz, including the auxiliary coprimality parameter, by the prime theorem in small progressions and the divisor bound for primes dividing that parameter. Below $x^{.499}$ use fixed prime product Bombieri–Vinogradov, for example Liu–Park–Song Theorem 3.2 for the two disjoint prime intervals.

For positive upper bounds, use disjoint short rectangles with coordinate mesh ratio $1+\eta_0$ and retain every rectangle meeting the dyadic hyperbolic interval. Their union lies in the original interval enlarged by $O(\eta_0 x)$ at its two ends. The longer prime identifier has uniform Siegel–Walfisz on intervals by subtracting prefix estimates. Across rectangles and dyadic modulus blocks the logarithmic losses are bounded powers for each fixed $\eta_0>0$. The primitive discrepancies sum to $O_A(x L^{-A})$. The PNT mass of the enlarged union is at most $(a_E+O(\eta_0)+o(1))x/(2L)$. Take $x\to\infty$ before $\eta_0\downarrow0$. This supplies the two positive sieve applications without a modulus-dependent boundary loss.

All primes of the sieve moduli actually used are less than $x^{.291}$, hence none can divide the semiprime input. The primitive main on odd moduli is exactly $1/\varphi(h)$ times the total mass. Even moduli have no incidence on these odd inputs for the sieve of $k+2$. The dimension-one local product is $V(z)=\prod_{2<r<z}(1-1/(r-1))\sim \mathfrak S_2e^{-\gamma}/\log z$. The linear upper sieve has $F(s)=2e^\gamma/s$ for $1\le s\le3$.

Apply it first to $P^-(k+2)>x^{.21}$ with level $x^{.504}$. The sieve parameter is $2.4$. Multiplication by $L$ gives normalized mass at most $(2/.504)a_E+o(1)$.

## The complementary pairs

Every exceptional divisor $M=rs$ is a product of distinct primes exceeding $x^{.21}$. For all sufficiently large $x$ its logarithm divided by $L$ lies in $[.5-3\epsilon,.5+3\epsilon]$. Its two factors each have exponent in $[.21,.291]$. Over all such $M$, Mertens' theorem applied to both variables bounds

$$
\limsup\sum_M\frac1{\varphi(M)}\le
\frac{(.291-.21)6\epsilon}{2(.21)^2}.
$$

The denominator two accounts for ordering. The strip has the displayed width for each fixed first exponent. Divide by two again at the final counting step, since the two complementary products represent one failed partition.

For each $M$ impose $M\mid k+2$ and remove small prime factors of $k+2$ at threshold $x^{.001}$ using an upper linear sieve of level $x^{.002}$. All original rough outputs survive. For every sieve divisor $d$, $(M,d)=1$ and $Md< x^{.504}$. The two prime factors of $M$ exceed $x^{.21}$ and the factors of $d$ are at most $x^{.002}$. Thus $Md$ recovers both parts uniquely. The full sum of sieve remainders is bounded by a single mean of the absolute discrepancies. Equivalently apply the linear sieve once to the nonnegative aggregate weight counting the permitted divisors $M$ of each $k+2$. All unrestricted $d\le x^{.002}$ also satisfy the same recovery. With $s=2$ the normalized upper is $(2/.002)a_E\sum_M1/\varphi(M)+o(1)$. Including the complementary-pair factor yields

$$
\limsup U_{E,4}/S^\circ\le
500 a_E\frac{.081\cdot6\epsilon}{2(.21)^2}
=2.2045166596\ldots\cdot10^{-8}.
$$

Combining the two bounds proves the assertions above. No upper for another source is allocated to this slab.

## Sources

- Theorem 1.1 and its overlap following the theorem. [Fouvry and Radziwiłł](https://arxiv.org/html/1812.00562v2)
- Theorem 3.2 on products of distinct primes. [Liu, Park and Song](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~pspark/boundedgaps.pdf)
- Lemma 2.5, upper and lower linear sieve. [Matomäki and Zuniga-Alterman](https://www.utupub.fi/bitstream/handle/10024/185534/Matom%C3%A4ki_and_zuniga_weighted_sieves_2025.pdf?sequence=1)

# Reweighting every near-threshold input owner on the balanced triple source

Use $L=\log x$, $U=x^\alpha$, $D=x^d$, $\alpha=.24$, $d=.49$, $b=d-\alpha=.25$, $w=\exp(L^a)$ for fixed $0<a<1$, and $I=(x/2,x]$. Let $g(n)=2$ on the squarefree three-prime outputs in the original Gold 4.63 family, all coordinates $\log r/\log n\in(.2001,.4999)$, and zero elsewhere. Its native outside coefficient is $-g$. Write $J_C$ for its ordinary mass in units $x/(2L)$. The source-level inequality below uses $S^\circ=\mathfrak S_2x/(2L)\sim S_b$.

For $n=k+2\in I$, restrict to $w$-rough squarefree $k$ and use this restriction on every displayed physical sum. Put $P=\{p\mid k:U<p\le x^b,\ p\ \mathrm{prime}\}$, $m=|P|$, let $Q$ be the product of the prime divisors of $k$ greater than $x^b$, and $s$ the product of those at most $U$. Write $M_s(v)=\sum_{e\mid s,\ e\le v}\mu(e)$ and take this as zero for $v<1$. Define

$$
 b^*(k)=-\log Q\,M_s(U)+\sum_{p\in P}(\log k-\log p)M_s(D/p)
                  +1_{\mathbb P}(k)\log k.
$$

The complete native contribution $W_C=-\sum g(k+2)B_\sigma(k)$ satisfies

$$
\frac{W_C}{S^\circ}
=\underbrace{\frac{2-d}{d}\log\frac{d-\alpha}{\alpha}}_{0.12579839127670\ldots}\,J_C
 -\frac{1}{S^\circ}\sum g(k+2)b^*(k)+o(1).
\tag{1}
$$

This includes every input rank and prime boundary. For $1<s\le U$ the residual $b^*$ vanishes on every configuration. For $s=1$ it equals $(m-1)\log k+1_{\mathbb P}(k)\log k$. In particular every input with one near-threshold prime and $s\le U$, including genuine semiprimes of this shape, disappears from the residual. Reweighting creates the *positive* surface debit in (1). Outputs on other chambers retain their original contribution. Only the net right-hand side can enter a terminal bound.

## Exact divisor accounting

For an eligible label $p$ write $C_p$ for its complete native inner divisor sum without $\log p$. When $k$ is composite, summing all divisors of $k/p$ gives zero. Thus $C_p$ is the negative of the sum with divisor at most $a_p=\max(U,D/p)$. For $p\in P$, any such divisor uses zero or one other prime in $P$, and none in $Q$. If it uses $p'\in P$ then its remaining divisor is at most $D/(pp')\le x^{.01}$. It follows that

$$
 C_p=-M_s(D/p)+\sum_{j\in P\setminus\{p\}} M_s(D/(pj)),\qquad
 C_q=-M_s(U)\quad(q\mid Q).
$$

For a genuine prime $k$ the original row is zero. It has $s=1,m=0,Q=k$ and the explicit prime term in $b^*$ supplies the required correction. Addition over all original labels gives the finite identity

$$
 B_\sigma(k)-\sum_{p\in P}\log k\,C_p
 = b^*(k)-\sum_{\{p,j\}\subset P}(2\log k-\log(pj)) M_s(D/(pj)).
\tag{2}
$$

When $s>1$ and $s\le U$, $M_s(v)=0$ for every $v\ge U$. When $s=1$ these terms equal one. The residual evaluations follow.

## Small moduli and the boundary principal

On the actual balanced output family the absolute sum of progression discrepancies in the reduced residue $2$ over odd moduli $h\le x^{.495}$ is $O_A(xL^{-A})$ for every $A$, also with an interval prefix. This follows from Liu–Park–Song Theorem 3.2 on boxes in three distinct primes. One can cut the prime exponents $\log r_i/L$ at mesh $L^{-K}$. All faces comparing $\log r_i$ and $\log n$ are linear. Dyadic ends of the product are handled by the product cutoff or interval collars. The PNT estimate in intervals with polynomial prime size, after partial summation in two variables, bounds the crossing collars by $O_B(xL^{-B})$ on taking $K$ large. Under the discrepancy sum their actual incidence is at most $(\#\mathrm{collar})^{1/2}(\sum_{k\le x}\tau(k)^2)^{1/2}$ and the primitive term costs $O(L)$ times the collar population. The fixed power of $L$ boxes is absorbed in the log precision. This is the same bounded-profile transfer as Gold 4.66 at a fixed gap below one half.

Use this estimate after expanding $R_w(k)$. Truncate Bonferroni at $O_A(\log L)$ factors and apply its two adjacent orders to the absolute unsigned remainder. A sieve divisor of primes at most $w$ has size $x^{o(1)}$ at these orders. The presieve factor and the $w$-rough part of a modulus are uniquely recovered. The unsieved incidence in the first sum of (2) has modulus $pe\le D$, with $p\in P$ and $e\le D/p$; there are at most two eligible labels in a modulus of this size. In the pair term the modulus is $pje\le D$ with $e\le x^{.01}$ and the two larger primes are uniquely recovered as an unordered pair. For physical rows $e$ may be recovered inside the squarefree integers. Removing or restoring the squarefree restriction on $w$-rough integers costs $O_A(xL^{-A})$ by Cauchy–Schwarz from $O(x/w)$ squareful integers, $\sum\tau(k)^2\ll xL^3$, and the bounded number of prime divisors greater than $x^{.24}$. The squareful deletion also permits using ordinary product moduli in place of an incidence defined only on squarefree inputs. In the first sum explicitly restrict $(p,e)=1$, which is exact on squarefree $k$. The factorial Bonferroni tail is smaller than any prescribed inverse log power after allowing for the fixed powers of $L$ in the coefficient sums. Prefix partial summation supplies $\log k$.

Put $g_w=\prod_{2<r\le w}(1-1/(r-1))$ and let $A_w(T)=\sum_{u\le T,\ u\ \mathrm{odd}}\mu(u)R_w(u)/\varphi(u)$. For a modulus containing $p$ or another prime forbidden by primitive coprimality with the output or the selected label, deleting terms of $A_w$ containing that prime costs $O(Lx^{-.19})$ per excluded factor. There are at most four such factors. The corresponding deletion in the prime sums costs the same type of power saving. The excluded factors of the output exceed $x^{.19}$ and the pair cutoff for $e$ is less than $x^{.01}$.

For the first sum in (2), complementary divisors produce the primitive inner factor $A_w(D/p)$, up to the preceding exclusions. Its argument is at least $x^{.24}$. The Möbius PNT and subpower convolution give $A_w(D/p)=O_A(L^{-A})$ uniformly here. Hence the average of the entire first sum against $g$ is $o(S^\circ)$. In this application the replacing logarithm is $\log k$, which depends only on the product endpoint. Input ownership remains complete.

For the pair term the corresponding primitive factor is $A_w(D/(pj))$. Its argument can be one. That boundary contributes at leading order. The signed measures
$$
 d\mu_x(v)=g_w L A_w(x^v)\,dv,\qquad v\ge0,
$$
have uniformly bounded total variation and converge weakly to $\mathfrak S_2\delta_0$. To see this let $A$ omit the presieve in $A_w$. The Euler series for $\mu(u)/\varphi(u)$ on odd integers is $G(z)/\zeta(1+z)$, with $G(0)=\mathfrak S_2$ and an absolutely summable correction with some positive power moment. The classical Möbius prime number theorem implies $A(e^v)=O_B((1+v)^{-B})$ for all fixed $B$. Its integral over $v\ge0$ is $\mathfrak S_2$, by taking $z\downarrow0$ in the Laplace transform $G(z)/(z\zeta(1+z))$. The inverse Euler factors for $2<p\le w$ form a positive Dirichlet series $h_w$ of total mass $g_w^{-1}$. The normalized law of $\log d$ with weight $g_w h_w(d)$ has tail $O(\exp(-cL/\log w))$ above each fixed $cL$, because $g_w\sum_d h_w(d)d^{1/\log w}\ll1$. Indeed $\sum_{p\le w}(p^{1/\log w}-1)/p\ll1$, and the finitely many small-prime factors are uniformly bounded for large $w$. Convolution with the integrable signed kernel $A(e^v)$ proves the assertion, including total variation outside each fixed neighborhood of zero.

Use the PNT twice to replace $\sum_{p,j}$ by $dt\,du/(tu)$, where $t=\log p/L$, $u=\log j/L$. For a fully uniform replacement first expand $A_w(D/(pj))$ over $e\le x^{.01}$. The remaining moving upper endpoint $pj\le D/e$ and the bounded polynomial in $\log(pj)/L$ permit ordinary partial summation, with arbitrary log precision uniformly in $e$. The sum of the absolute $e$ coefficients is $O(L)$. Removing the diagonal and changing $1/(p-1)$ to $1/p$ cost a power saving. Divide by two for unordered pairs. For fixed $n$ the primitive sum is consequently
$$
\frac12\int_0^{d-2\alpha}
\left(2\frac{\log k}{L}-d+v\right)
\left(\int_{\alpha}^{d-v-\alpha}\frac{dt}{t(d-v-t)}\right)d\mu_x(v)+o(1).
$$
The inner integral is continuous at zero. The bounded variation estimate pays $\log k/L=1+O(1/L)$ uniformly on the dyadic interval. In the limit this equals $\mathfrak S_2(2-d)d^{-1}\log((d-\alpha)/\alpha)$. Summing against $g$ and using its PNT mass proves (1).

## Direct adversarial test and the first unpaid term

At $x=10^9$ the following actual balanced outputs certify both residual signs when $s>U$. For example take the fixed presieve exponent $a=1/20$, for which $w<5$ at this $x$.

| $k$ | $s$ | $Q$ | $n=k+2$ | $b^*(k)$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $500253215$ | $5\cdot7\cdot11$ | $1299359$ | $359\cdot409\cdot3407$ | $-\log Q$ |
| $500237699$ | $13\cdot17$ | $2263519$ | $463\cdot929\cdot1163$ | $+\log Q$ |

These are finite tests of signs. They also disprove a uniform pointwise completion claiming $b^*\ge0$ on this class of inputs. They do not give a density on an infinite sequence of scales. To close this approach one still needs a signed mean for $s>U$ and the $s=1,m=0$ composite inputs. Estimating the computable low-divisor pieces of $b^*$ eventually exposes $1_{\mathbb P}(k)\log k$ on the balanced three-prime output. Its independent favorable lower bound is precisely prime-sensitive information not supplied by (1).

## Independent rival bound for the whole rank-four semiprime-input row

For rank-four outputs the retained part $F$ is zero. A nonzero $f$ requires a squarefree good output and $H\ne0$. The exact native small-prime cancellation and good-set gap imply every output coordinate $t_i>1/5-\epsilon$ (`FMGoodSupport.lean`, `small_prime_cancels` and `gap_excluded`). All four coordinates are below $.401$. If each $t_i>1/5$, then $-f$ equals the complementary-pair count of the first packet. If a coordinate falls in $(1/5-\epsilon,1/5]$, the native lower $H\ge-3$ bounds $-f\le3$. The signs and the degree-two kernel follow directly from the native divisor sum. No omitted off-good rank-four residual is added.

The angular mass $J_4^-$ of the complete nonnegative function $-f$ on rank four is therefore at most $10\epsilon$. Here is an explicit volume bound. For a chosen singleton collar coordinate, its interval has width $\epsilon$, the other three have exponents at least $.199$, and the area of the remaining positive simplex is at most $(1-(.2-\epsilon)-3(.199))^2/2$. Divide by $4! (.199)^4$ and multiply by 12 for the four choices and weight three. If there is no singleton collar, for each of three pair partitions two coordinates can be integrated in intervals of length $.101$ and the third in an interval of width $4\epsilon$. Divide by $4! (.2)^4$ and multiply by three. The two coefficients of $\epsilon$ are less than 6.57 and 3.19 respectively.

Now reverse the source and sieve $k=n-2$ for every prime factor at most $x^{.24}$. On the complete semiprime-input contribution, both factors of $k$ must exceed $x^{.24}$ for the physical coefficient to be nonzero, and each such coefficient is $-\log k$. Count the larger rough population with the same nonnegative output envelope. It is an angular profile of four polynomially large primes with fixed polyhedral boundaries, so the same source version of Liu–Park–Song gives fixed level $\theta<1/2$. Primitive coprimality with an output prime of size $>x^{.19}$ costs $o(x/L^A)$ in the summed main term by $\sum_{d\le D,p\mid d}1/\varphi(d)\ll L/(p-1)$. Letting $\theta\uparrow1/2$ in the upper linear sieve gives
$$
0\le\limsup \frac{U_{\mathrm{semiprime},4}}{S^\circ}\le4J_4^-<4\cdot10^{-8}.

# Unmarked rough companions and the rank-one gap

The estimates below apply to the actual primes \(x<p\le 2x\). They quantify the part of the perforated polynomial sieve on which every Lü–Wang–Wu auxiliary product vanishes. They also give a lower bound there for companions having at least three distinct prime factors.

Write \(L=\log x\), \(M(F)=\sum_{x<p\le 2x}(\log p)F(p+2)\), \(R_0(n)=1_{P^-(n)>x^\beta}\), and
\[
 V_0=\prod_{2<q\le x^\beta}\left(1-\frac1{q-1}\right)
 \sim \frac{2e^{-\gamma}C_2}{\beta L}.
\]
The products here and below range over primes. Take \(D=x^{.001}\), \(s=.001/\beta\) large and fixed. Let \(R\) be the sieve with the \(H\) fixed exceptional subpower bands in ETH-PERF-01 and \(V\) its local product. Write \(\theta_s=C s^{-s/2}\) with an absolute sieve constant, enlarging \(C\) a fixed number of times if necessary.

## Mass invisible to the marks

The fundamental lemma in Koukoulopoulos, *The Distribution of Prime Numbers*, Theorem 19.1(a)–(c), gives upper and lower divisor polynomials supported on squarefree odd \(d\le D\), with coefficients of absolute value at most one. The local density is \(1/(q-1)\). The inverse dimension-one product condition on all prime intervals holds uniformly for either choice of omitted bands. Ordinary prime Bombieri–Vinogradov on the reduced progression \(-2\bmod d\) gives
\[
 (1-\theta_s+o(1))xV_0\le M(R_0)\le(1+\theta_s+o(1))xV_0.
\]
The same applies to \(R,V\). Each omitted band contributes a factor \(2+o(1)\) to \(V/V_0\) by Mertens' theorem. Consequently,
\[
 \frac{M(R_0)}{M(R)}
     =2^{-H}\big(1+O(\theta_s)+o(1)\big).
\]
All estimates take \(x\) to infinity after fixing \(H,\beta\). With \(s\) fixed the bracket in this display cannot be replaced by an established \(1+o(1)\).

On every input selected by \(R_0\), all exceptional band counts vanish for large \(x\), and hence every marked product \(W_j\) vanishes pointwise. Every linear combination \(G\) of functions \(W_jS_j\), with arbitrary finite divisor-polynomial tests \(S_j\), obeys
\[
 \frac{M(R|G-1|^2)}{M(R)}\ \ge\ \frac{M(R_0)}{M(R)}.
\]
The observation holds for any function of the marked products that vanishes when its arguments are all zero. Thus normalization by the much larger perforated sieve mass can make the missing fraction small, while the absolute error on the unmarked set still has size \(xV_0\).

## Actual high-rank supply on the unmarked set

For the three exponent intervals \((2,4],(5,10],(11,22]\) let \(\mathcal B_j\) consist of the primes whose \(\log q/(\beta L)\) belongs to the respective interval. Set \(t_j(n)=\#\{q\in\mathcal B_j:q\mid n\}\), \(Y=t_1t_2t_3\), and \(m=\log 2\). For \(h=1,2\) write
\[
 F_1=m^3,\qquad F_2=(m+m^2)^3.
\]
Then
\[
 (1-\theta_s)F_h+o(1)
 \le \frac{M(R_0Y^h)}{xV_0}
 \le(1+\theta_s)F_h+o(1).
\]

To prove these inequalities, multiply the two fundamental-lemma divisor polynomials for \(R_0\) by the nonnegative \(Y^h\) and expand. Each \(t_j^2=t_j+2\binom{t_j}{2}\). The squarefree prime product specifying the selected primes in the three bands determines all three unordered subsets. The remaining sieve divisor has primes at most \(x^\beta\), so the folded modulus has one representation with coefficient bounded by eight. All moduli are \(\le x^{.001+72\beta}\), where \(72=2(4+10+22)\). This lies within ordinary prime Bombieri–Vinogradov for our choice \(\beta<.001\). Its absolute error is \(O_A(xL^{-A})\). In the local model the disjoint primes divide independently with probabilities \(v_q=1/(q-1)\). For each band \(\sum v_q=m+o(1)\) and \(\sum v_q^2=o(1)\). The first two raw local moments of \(t_j\) converge to \(m\) and \(m+m^2\). Products across the disjoint bands factor, which proves the displayed estimates.

A squareful \(p+2\) in \(R_0\) has \(q^2\mid p+2\) with \(q>x^\beta\); an integer count bounds its prime log mass by \(O(L(x^{1-\beta}+\sqrt{x}))\). As \(Y^2\) is bounded in terms of fixed \(\beta\) on \(n\le 3x\), deleting this part costs \(o(xV_0)\) in both moments. Cauchy's inequality on the positive squarefree measure now gives
\[
 \liminf_{x\to\infty}
 \frac{M(R_0\mu^2\,1_{Y>0})}{xV_0}
 \ \ge\
 \frac{(1-\theta_s)^2}{1+\theta_s}
 \left(\frac{m}{1+m}\right)^3 .
\]
For sufficiently small \(\beta\) we have \(\theta_s\le 1/10\). Since \(\log 2>2/3\), the right side exceeds
\[
 \frac{(9/10)^2}{11/10}(2/5)^3=\frac{324}{6875}>\frac1{25}.
\]
Every counted companion has at least three distinct polynomial-sized prime factors and has no prime below \(x^\beta\). All these companions lie in the zero set of every \(W_j\).

## Consequences for the attempted lift

The elementary dimension-two upper-bound sieve on \(p(p+2)\) bounds the actual twin log mass by \(C_0 x/L\) with an absolute \(C_0\). In the last inequality \(1/25\) is independent of \(\beta\), while \(xV_0\sim 2e^{-\gamma}C_2 x/(\beta L)\). Decreasing fixed \(\beta\) makes the lower bound for the genuine undifferentiated high-rank population exceed any fixed multiple of this upper bound for twins. The argument gives no allocation between odd and even rank within this population.

For a precise information bound, keep the actual prime log weights, masks, ranks, and every unsigned observation fixed. Consider the two *comparison signs* that agree with arithmetic \(\mu\) elsewhere and take the respective constant values \(+1,-1\) on \(R_0\mu^2\,1_{Y>0}\). Every observed signed quantity of the form \(M(\mu\,W_jS_j)\) has exactly the same value for the two choices. Their unmarked signed composite totals differ by more than \((2/25+o(1))xV_0\). This construction diagnoses the information carried by these particular marked statistics. Only the original Möbius sign is asserted to be arithmetic.

On the actual integers the missing rank-sensitive inequality has a direct expression. With \(T\) the genuine twin log mass on \((x,2x]\) and \(\Omega\) counting prime factors with multiplicity,
\[
 T=M(R_0\,1_{\mu=-1})-M(R_0\,1_{\mu=-1,\ \Omega\ge3}).
\]
The second term includes all squarefree odd-rank composites, while nonsquarefree companions make zero contribution to both terms on the right. All twins survive \(R_0\) for large \(x\). A positive lower bound for this difference on an unbounded sequence would supply the terminal theorem. Neither the marked cancellation estimate nor the positive high-rank estimate gives that lower bound.

### Forcing the missing prime labels by multiplication

One possible way to make a marker nonzero on the blind sector is to multiply \(p+2\) by selected marking primes before evaluating its Möbius and occupancy weights. On the actual no-hole sector this has an exact formula, including for a weighted average over multipliers. For each \(x\), take any finite family \(\mathcal A_x\) of squarefree integers whose prime factors are \(\le x^\beta\) and complex scalars \(c_a\). Write \(\boldsymbol\omega_E\) for the vector of the \(H\) exceptional band occupancies. Let \(F\) be any function of this vector, and let \(Z(n)\) be any bounded arithmetic test on the original companion. Then
\[
 \sum_{a\in\mathcal A_x}c_a\!
 \sum_{x<p\le2x}(\log p)R_0(p+2)Z(p+2)\,
      \mu\big(a(p+2)\big)F\big(\boldsymbol\omega_E(a(p+2))\big)
 =
 \left[\sum_{a\in\mathcal A_x}c_a\mu(a)F(\boldsymbol\omega_E(a))\right]
 M(R_0Z\mu).
\]
Indeed \(R_0(n)\) implies \((a,n)=1\), and all the selected bands lie below \(x^\beta\) for large \(x\). Hence multiplication contributes exactly the external prime labels, leaving the original companion with none. The argument holds also with an \(a\)-dependent \(F_a\). It is an exact identity at each sufficiently large scale, with no growth restriction on the number of multipliers or their coefficients. Zero bracket gives the identity \(0=0\). A nonzero bracket gives precisely the original unmarked signed statistic upon division. Thus forced multiplicative labels create no independent equation on the missing object, even if one forces one label in every group and makes all auxiliary products nonzero.

The reason the published marked correlation cannot estimate this new left side is also visible before averaging. Its shift-two prime source is \(p+2\) with input \(p\). Replacing the argument by \(a(p+2)=ap+2a\) replaces the corresponding input at shift \(2a\) by \(ap\), composite for \(a>1\). In the label-extraction step the forced divisibility \(a\mid a(p+2)\) puts no congruence condition on \(p+2\). The independent labels in LWW (4.5)–(4.8), used in the mean-square estimate, are not supplied by these repetitions.

The comparison-sign changes above also preserve any unmarked bounded signed test known only up to \(o(x/L^\alpha)\) for fixed \(\alpha<1\). Their effect is \(O_\beta(x/L)=o(x/L^\alpha)\). This remains true uniformly over all divisor polynomials \(S(n)=\sum_{d\mid n}l_d\) with \(\lvert l_d\rvert\le1\) in absolute value. On the perturbed squarefree \(n\le3x\) every prime factor is above \(x^\beta\), hence \(\tau(n)\le 2^{2/\beta}\) for large \(x\). The total variation argument is at fixed \(\beta\). It covers the coarse precision of the global HLC estimate but does not claim invariance for unknown unmarked estimates of terminal precision.

**Primary sources.** The upper and lower sieve weights and their dimension bound come from Koukoulopoulos, Theorem 19.1. The auxiliary weights and their pointwise marked factors come from Lü–Wang–Wu (2.6)–(2.14). ## A smaller absolute four-factor cost

For any retained rectangular angular cell of fixed rank \(r\ge3\), all prime factors exceed a common fixed positive power of \(x\) and the least satisfies \(p_1\le x^{1/3}\). Pascadi's Proposition 5.2 accepts \(x^{2\tau}\le N\le x^{1/3+\tau}\) for every sufficiently small fixed \(\tau>0\). The whole two-sieve and factorization proof for the five boxes in native_rough_sieve applies to this least prime also. Take \(\tau\) smaller than one fourth of the common lower exponent. The prime short coefficient satisfies Siegel–Walfisz uniformly over the fixed cells, the other \(r-1\) primes give a coefficient bounded by \((r-1)!\), and the count of dyadic cells is a fixed power of \(\log x\). Cells meeting the support and their upper products preserve the exponent slack. Take \(x\to\infty\) first, then the small-sieve and \(\tau\) limits. The same conclusion holds at rank two when the smaller prime is in either narrow band about \(x^{1/5}\). For the near-half rank-two band we retain the separate \(32/9\) inequality. Rank-dependent constants cause no limit exchange since the rough tail has a fixed finite rank ceiling. [Pascadi, Propositions 4.4 and 5.2](https://arxiv.org/html/2505.00653v2)

For the rank-four angular error envelope keep the dependence of each convolution on its *own* prime-sum mass. The proof in collar_ledger gives

\[
K_h(v)\le\frac{h}{v}\log^{h-1}(v/\delta)
\]

+\frac{4\epsilon C_2^2}{\beta(1-\beta)}
=0.00001960713760979619438614\ldots

D_t=\frac73\,\frac{4\cdot54^{255}}{255!(1-54/256)}
<2.034\cdot10^{-62}.

\[
B_0=\frac{\epsilon}{a_0(1-a_0)}
+\frac{\epsilon^2}{2a_0^2(3/5)}
+\frac{3(5\epsilon)^4}{5!\,4!\,a_0^5},\qquad
I_0=\epsilon/[\nu(1-\nu)] .
\]

Here \(A_0\) bounds the positive good-sector mass from near-half rank two. \(B_0\) bounds the positive good-sector masses from the other rank-two band, rank three, and rank five, respectively. The rank-five term uses all prime orders and the full native upper height three. Good rank four and all higher positive ranks vanish. The omitted (off-good) rank-two source is nonnegative and has ordinary mass at most \(I_0\). Put \(D_m=9\delta^{-2}/(50\,99!)<3.086\cdot10^{-134}\). This is the combined signed calibration debit for the original \(H-K_X\), with the general \(q\) bank, no truncation in rank, and the squarefree filter.

The exact native identity after the \(o(S_b)\) prime-power, ordinary mean and Vaughan payments is

\[
\frac{\mathcal U+T}{S_b}
=1+\frac{B(P)-A(P)-R_2-R_4-R_{\rm tail}
+\operatorname{deviation}(\mathrm{calibrated})}{S_b}+o(1).
\]

The good contribution lies between \(-[(23/9)A_0+(7/3)B_0]\) and \(A_0+B_0\), up to \(o(1)\). The sign multiplying the omitted pair is minus, so its interval is \([-(7/3)I_0, I_0]\). \[
\begin{aligned}
L_0&=1-\tfrac{23}9 A_0-\tfrac73(B_0+I_0)-D_4-D_t-D_m
 =0.99995420040113248509504115422\ldots,\\

 =1.00004577048775628226606863364\ldots .

\[
\begin{aligned}
L_0-\tfrac73j_+-o(1)&\le v+t\le U_0+j_++o(1),\\
L_0+j_- -o(1)&\le v+t+b\le U_0+j_++o(1).
\end{aligned}
\]

Numerically the first interval is \([0.35688065890063996379504\ldots,\,1.27564871684511021996607\ldots]\). Its upper end bounds \(v\) unconditionally by \(t\ge0\). The second interval starts at \(1.27543154218178365097504\ldots\). The sufficient closing condition is a strict improvement on \(\limsup v<L_0-(7/3)j_+\), still unproved. The Gold 4.66 full proof, §6 (6.1), uses \(J\le.28449989344325252602\) on the same full boxes. # An obstruction for nonpositive owner rows under a scalar smooth prefix

Let v>0, A>0 satisfy A+v<1/2, and let h be smooth from the right at zero, h(0)=1 and h(t)=0 for t≥A. Put B=1−v. In the smoothed Vaughan sum with owner prime ℓ>x^v, the inner tail for a nonunit squarefree cofactor carrying exponents t_i is the negative of its Boolean finite difference

    G_h(t_1,…,t_m) = Σ_{S⊆[m]} (−1)^|S| h(Σ_{i∈S}t_i).

Consider the proposed sufficient pointwise sign G_h≥0 for all such exponent profiles with Σt_i<B. This quantifier is a relaxation independent of the shifted output. Near-coincident exponents may be obtained by continuity from distinct exponents. Ordinary PNT in the individual fixed exponent intervals and one final dyadic prime interval realizes arbitrary interior limits for input rows if desired. It does not control the factorization of the shifted output.

**Slope theorem.** This pointwise condition forces −h′(0)≥3/(2A). The unavoidable comparator charge of this device exceeds 3 units per unit of the ordinary positive profile mass.

Indeed, for w=1−h the two-coordinate differences state w(s+t)≤w(s)+w(t) whenever s,t>0 and s+t<B. Splitting t into m equal pieces and sending m→∞ gives w(t)≤tw′(0+). For four increments just above A/2 their total remains less than B, because 2A<1−v. Every subset of size ≥2 lies outside the support, so G_h=1−Σ_i h(t_i)≥0. Sending all t_i↓A/2 yields w(A/2)≥3/4. The two estimates imply the asserted slope bound. With the genuine prime boundary included, the principal term relating this smoothed sum to the original contains the additional multiple (1−v)(−h′(0)) of the actual comparator. The harmonic Möbius transform and its linear term at zero are derived in the companion Mellin note. In particular (1−v)·3/(2A)>3. The unchanged prime-side upper already costs 7/3 on positive ordinary profile mass. Universal pointwise sign by this mechanism cannot improve that coefficient.

**Quantified failure if a smaller slope is chosen.** If all pair differences are nonnegative and (1−v)(−h′(0))≤7/3, then by the same pair test h(A/2)≥1−7A/(6(1−v)). As 2A<1−v, the four-label G_h near A/2+ is strictly below −2/3 in the limit. By continuity an open four-label region has strictly positive raw owner weight there. This proves a geometric counterexample to the proposed pointwise simplification. It does not assert that any native joint f-positive shifted population has positive lower density. If a proof avoids the four-label deficit by violating the pair condition, its two-label signed deficit must be paid instead.

The hypothesis is intentionally specific. Signed joint estimates, additional label-dependent annihilators and native output-dependent restrictions can evade it. No bound on the unknown signed remainder is inferred from this theorem.

evidence.text:
# A polynomial input presieve for the unaltered signed FM outside coefficient

Set L=log x, U=V=x^.24 and D=x^.49. Keep every prime label, strict threshold and squarefree condition in the native signed large-product coefficient B(k), with k=n−2. For h≥2 write

    C_h(f) = Σ_{x/2<n≤x} f_x(n) 1_{P⁻(k)>h} μ²(k) B(k).

The bounded output f may be the native Φ, ψ, Φ−ψ, or their positive or negative parts. For large x it has bounded rank and P⁻(n)>x^ζ on its support, ζ=1/(4·10^11), and ∑|f|≪_f x/L. Its signed and unsigned profiles satisfy the primitive product progression estimate proved in uniform_native_transfer.md, including common upper endpoints. All normalized sums use S_b∼S₂x/(2L).

**Theorem.** Fix 0<a<1 and w=exp(L^a). Then

    lim_{ε↓0} limsup_{x→∞} |C_w(f)−C_{x^ε}(f)|/S_b = 0.

In particular, for any requested error one can keep only squarefree physical inputs with every prime above one fixed power of x and with rank at most ⌊1/ε⌋. This is collective cancellation over the actual sharp tagged sum, including all original owners. It makes no statement about the sum of absolute row weights or an independently selected tag mask. The small-power exponent is chosen before letting x grow.

## Sieve cost with a fixed polynomial threshold

Write z=x^ε with fixed 0<ε<ζ. Apply the exact Vaughan identity used in uniform_native_transfer.md with the same original U,V,D. Prime inputs have weight θ(k) in either presieve. The proper powers and rough nonsquarefree inputs are negligible after the absolute divisor bound, since repeated primes now exceed z. It suffices to evaluate the same two Type I terms and the short product. Their moduli e₀≤x^.49 have no prime ≤z. The primitive progression is n≡2 mod e₀. Coefficients with the common factors log k extracted by partial summation are bounded by O(L) after grouping. For the short and Λ convolution sums this follows from Σ_{j|e₀}Λ(j)=log e₀. The positivity comparison can use the sum of the absolute ungrouped coefficients with the same O(L) bound.

For each e₀ sieve k/e₀ by the odd primes up to z, using the two dimension-one fundamental-lemma weights λ^± of level x^.002. They bracket the integer presieve pointwise. For each sign of the profile and coefficient, the total progression errors follow from the profile progression bound at level x^.492. In fact the representation e₀d is unique because primes of d are ≤z and primes of e₀ exceed z. The maximum cumulative coefficient is O(L), and the common weight log k costs one partial summation. All active n are coprime to d, so the sole remaining primitive exclusion is (n,e₀)=1. The main sum of λ^±(d)/φ(d) is g_z(1+O(E_s)) uniformly, where g_z=∏_{2<p≤z}(1−1/(p−1)), s=.002/ε, E_s≪s^(−s/2) as s→∞ with an absolute dimension-one constant. The dimension follows from the Mertens product for 1/(p−1) away from 2. The same upper and lower weights handle positive and negative coefficients.

On rough moduli, Σ_{e₀≤x^.49} R_z(e₀)/φ(e₀) ≪ 1/ε. This follows by comparing the Euler product, including all prime powers, to ∏_{z<p≤x}(1−1/p)⁻¹ with a bounded convergent correction. Also g_z L≪1/ε. Summing the majorant cost, including ∑|f|≪_f S_b, pays O_f(ε⁻² E_s) S_b+o_{ε,f}(S_b). This fixed-ε estimate is essential. A positive power of L multiplying E_s at fixed ε would invalidate the limiting argument.

## The degree-zero and degree-one Möbius means

For m odd put R_z(m)=1_{P⁻(m)>z}, with R_z(1)=1. At fixed ε and bounded 0≤v≤1, define the rough harmonic Möbius prefix A_z(x^v)=Σ_{m≤x^v}μ(m)R_z(m)/φ(m). Then, writing t=v/ε,

    A_z(x^v) = ρ(t) + o_ε(1),
    (log z)⁻¹ Σ_{m≤x^v} μ(m)R_z(m)log m/φ(m)
        = tρ(t)−∫₀ᵗρ(u)du + o_ε(1),

uniformly in v. Indeed m has bounded squarefree rank at fixed ε. Expand by rank j, divide the unordered labeled counts by j!, and use Mertens' theorem separately in each normalized logarithmic prime coordinate. The reciprocal p−1 may replace p with o(1) error, and repeated prime coordinates cost o(1). For j≥1 the cumulative limit of a rank j positive measure is continuous. Common-endpoint convergence is therefore uniform on the compact interval; the mass at the unit is handled exactly. The signed limit is the finite series

    Σ_{j≤t} (−1)^j/j! ∫_{u_i≥1,Σu_i≤t} du₁⋯duⱼ/(u₁⋯uⱼ).

It equals 1 on [0,1], and multiplication of its boundary derivative by t=Σu_i gives tρ′(t)=−ρ(t−1) for t>1. This specifies the Dickman function. Partial summation yields the second relation. Its standard properties give ∫₀^∞ρ(t)dt=e^γ and factorial decay. For the latter, tρ(t)=∫_{t−1}ᵗρ(t′)dt′ and monotonicity suffice. Exclusion of the at most 256 prime divisors of n or nℓ changes these prefixes by o_ε(1), with the same normalization in the log moment. The cost is O_ε(Σ_{p|nℓ}1/(p−1))=o_ε(1) where ℓ>z. For the second displayed prefix one multiplies this absolute bound by O(1/ε).

## The signed transfer

Mertens gives g_z log z→S₂e^(−γ), with S₂=2∏_{p>2}(1−1/(p−1)²). Put t₀=.24/ε. The first Type I principal per output is g_z[A_n(U)log k−B_n(U)], with B_n now the logarithmic harmonic prefix. Its difference from S₂ has limsup bounded by a constant times ε⁻¹ρ(t₀)+∫_{t₀}^∞ρ. For the Λ subtraction the main prefix has argument U, and the factor from summing log ℓ/φ(ℓ^j) costs O(L). The exact common-prime term has an extra 1/ℓ and is negligible, since all ℓ>z and the harmonic absolute prefix is O(1/ε). For the short-product subtraction the two main arguments D/ℓ and U are at least U whenever nonempty. The monotonicity of ρ and uniform convergence bound their difference by 2ρ(t₀)+o_ε(1). Its common-prime correction is negligible for the same reason. Thus all remaining principal errors divided by S_b are bounded in limsup by

    O_f( ε⁻¹ρ(.24/ε) + ∫_{.24/ε}^∞ρ + ε⁻²E_{.002/ε} ).

This expression tends to zero with ε. The original w transfer equals the same prime sum minus S₂Σf, with o(S_b) error. Subtraction proves the theorem.

**Scope in the closing ledger.** After choosing ε sufficiently small one may attempt the fixed-rank, jointly polynomially rough ORIGINAL k and k+2 problem, with prescribed tolerance on its entire sharp complement. The physical semiprimes and all associated positive and negative output terms still occur. A favorable source-specific estimate for the retained core is required for a strictly positive twin reserve. A restriction on k alone inserted into f cannot invoke its original product progression bound.

Koukoulopoulos, The Distribution of Prime Numbers, Theorem 19.1 (two-sided fundamental lemma): https://dms.umontreal.ca/~koukoulo/documents/publications/primes.pdf
Liu, Park and Song, Theorem 3.2 (underlying bounded-rank prime product progression estimate): https://doi.org/10.1007/s40993-017-0089-3
Lagarias, Euler's constant: Euler's work and modern developments, Theorem 3.5.1 (Dickman integral): https://doi.org/10.1090/S0273-0979-2013-01423-X

# An explicit higher-rank core for the complete native signed source

For f=Φ−ψ fix any 0<a<1 in the original FM outside coefficient C_w(f). Let L=log x. The following uses fixed powers and keeps both signs of f. Given any tolerance η>0, there exist first 0<t<1/12 and then 0<e<min(t,ζ) for which

    limsup | C_w(f) − Σ_{x/2<n≤x} f_x(n) μ²(k) R_{x^e}(k)
                 1_{ω(k)≥3} D_t(k) | / S_b ≤ η,        k=n−2.

Use U=V=x^t, H=x^(.5−2t). For squarefree k let s be the product of its primes ≤U, let m count the prime divisors in (U,H], and define M_s(U)=Σ_{d|s,d≤U}μ(d). The explicit corrected coefficient for arbitrary squarefree k is

    D_t(k) = 1_{k prime} log k + [(m−1)log k + log s] M_s(U).

Thus both k and n are polynomially rough with fixed, finite ranks. The prime boundary is restored before projecting to rank ≥3. The theorem pays a controlled signed perturbation and a near-half semiprime population. It supplies no favorable estimate for the remaining signed core.

## Complete identity and legal correction

Put D=U². In this retuned Vaughan identity the short product is empty because both factors must exceed U. Every label ℓ>U has the full complement divisor prefix M_s(U), independent of ℓ, since every divisor d≤U has only primes ≤U. For a composite squarefree k the sum over d|k/ℓ has zero untruncated Möbius sum. The original coefficient on this representation is −log(k/s)M_s(U). When k is prime, restore +log k exactly. Add the centered measurement

    log k · Σ_{U<ℓ≤H,ℓ|k} Σ_{d|k/ℓ,d≤U} μ(d)

on the entire source, with both signs of f present. It is exactly m log k M_s(U). For the subpower input mask R_w its total is o_{t,f}(S_b). Indeed the combined modulus ℓd≤x^(.5−t) has a unique largest prime ℓ>U≥d. Fold the input presieve as in uniform_native_transfer.md, at fixed positive margin below 1/2. In the primitive principal after separating n and ℓ, the harmonic rough Möbius prefix is A_{nℓ,w}(U)=O_{B,t}(L^−B) for every B. Other factors cost at most a fixed power of L. The same retuned Vaughan principal is the native genuine prime sum minus S₂Σf+o_{t,f}(S_b), so the original sharp whole outside agrees with this retuned corrected whole outside up to o(S_b).

## Changing the input mask in the presence of the added measurement

At fixed t rerun sharp_polynomial_presieve.md with z=x^e and sieve-modulus level x^{t/2}. For the original retuned Type I terms e₀≤U²=x^{2t}, and for the probe e₀≤HU=x^(.5−t); with the smooth sieve divisor included every modulus is ≤x^(.5−t/2). The actual profile satisfies the same progression estimate. Absolute costs are O_t(e^−2 E(t/(2e))) in S_b units plus o at fixed e. The harmonic Möbius prefix at U is ρ(t/e)+o_e(1). The additional principal of the probe, including the log k weight, is O_t(e^−1ρ(t/e))+o_{t,e}(1) because Σ_{U<ℓ≤H}1/(ℓ−1) is O_t(1). The omitted squareful inputs with a repeated prime >w or >z are negligible under the divisor bound. The remaining first/second Type I errors tend to zero as e↓0 for this fixed t, exactly as in the original proof. This proves a collective signed approximation of the full corrected source; it uses no claim about separate physical rows surviving a retune.

## Prime, semiprime and higher-rank bookkeeping

For prime k, D_t(k)=0. If k=pq with p<q, then q>U on the dyadic range for large x. When p≤U, s=p and M_s(U)=0. When U<p≤H, s=1,m=1 for large x, since two primes ≤H cannot reach x/2−2; again D_t(k)=0. When p>H both factors exceed H and D_t(k)=−log k. For this last band bound ∣f∣ by its uniform bound and preserve the original output roughness P⁻(pq+2)>x^ζ. At fixed p the simultaneous upper sieve on q and pq+2 is ≪_ζ x/(pL²) uniformly for H<p≤√x and 0<t<1/12. For instance sieve odd primes through x^{min(ζ,.001)}, and use the ordinary upper large sieve with distribution length x/p≥x^.5. All such sieve primes are distinct from p. Multiplication by log k and summing 1/p over H<p≤√x gives O_f(log((1/2)/(1/2−2t)))S_b+o_t(S_b), with a constant independent of t. For all retained semiprimes the physical sum has now been estimated exactly or absolutely. For rank ≥3, 1<s≤U still implies M_s(U)=0. For s=1 the factor (m−1)log k can carry a substantial signed contribution through f and is retained.

For the stated η, choose t for the near-half cost and then e for the two analytic perturbations. Finally let x→∞ at these fixed parameters. This order does not allow a subpower cutoff to replace U inside this demonstration. Charges on all higher ranks, including s=1, remain inside D_t. Replacing this explicit higher-rank sum by a bound on its adverse part alone can destroy terminal capacity, as the separate subpower signed restoration calculation demonstrates.

# Paying the adverse rank-three sources in the fixed-power representation

Use the sets, parameter order and corrected coefficient of simultaneous_core.md. Write f=f₊−f₋ where both parts are nonnegative. Define the scalar B=1_prime(k)log k−log(k/s)M_s(U), the raw retuned coefficient, and the pair correction on squarefree k

    P_t(k) = Σ_{p<q≤U, pq>U, pq|k} log(k/(pq))
                 Σ_{d|k/(pq), d≤U} μ(d).

All p,q in this formula are primes, with each unordered pair used once. Use the following physical coefficient over every retained k:

    Z_t(k,n) = f₊(n)[B(k)−P_t(k)] − f₋(n)D_t(k).

At subpower input roughness the total differs from the original signed O by o_t(S_b). With the polynomial mask x^e the additional absolute difference of totals in the iterated limit is arbitrarily small. The fixed-rank-three sector of Z_t is pointwise nonpositive and the adverse rank-two sector costs O_f(t)S_b in limsup. This is an upper decomposition with an explicitly retained favorable companion. No uniform smallness for the remaining ranks follows.

For the pair correction, pqd≤x^{3t}. The common log k is available by the primitive common-prefix estimate; the other weight −log(pq) is fixed for a marked pair. Multiple pairs at a given modulus cost at most O(L²) representations. In the subpower-mask case absolute squareful deletion and the small-prime fold have arbitrary log savings. After factoring primitive 1/φ(pq), the inner sum with d coprime to npq is A_{npq,w}(U); it has arbitrary log savings uniformly. If squarefreeness is first dropped, the overlap terms at p|d or q|d have an additional factor at most 1/w in the primitive main. At fixed z=x^e the same overlap costs o_e(1) per normalized source. The remaining prefix is ρ(t/e)+o_e(1). For the sieve-envelope error sum the ungrouped primitive harmonic coefficients: allowing every pair z<p,q≤x^t costs O((1+log(t/e))²); the d sum costs O(1/e), and g_z L≪1/e. Under x^{t/2} small-prime sieve level the moduli remain below x^{3.5t}<x^{1/2}. Thus the extra error in S_b units is O_{t,f}((1+log(t/e))²[ρ(t/e)/e + E(t/(2e))/e²])+o_{t,e}(1). The two other transfers are established in simultaneous_core.md.

Write k=pqr squarefree in the dyadic window for a physical rank-three input. If all factors exceed U, then B=−log k, P_t=0, and D_t=(m−1)log k≥0 since three primes >H would exceed x. If exactly one factor lies below or at U, M_s=0 and P_t=0. If two such primes p,q have pq≤U, their four divisors give M_s=0 and P_t=0. If pq>U, their two singles give M_s=−1, the remaining prime r exceeds H, and B=D_t=P_t=log r. Three small primes cannot form k. Hence f₊(B−P_t)≤0 and −f₋D_t≤0 in every case. On rank two, P_t vanishes. All remaining adverse rank-two weight lies on the same near-half band of simultaneous_core.md; f₊ may supply an additional favorable rank-two term and is retained. On primes Z_t=0. In particular an upper on Ω(k)≥4 without the favorable lower-rank terms is a valid sufficient route if it is independently small enough. Its magnitude must be established, with all constants in t recorded, before it can improve the numerical full bound.

## Finite extensions and their cost

For any fixed integer J≥2 choose t<min(1/12,1/(3(J+1))). For i=2,…,J add the full-source zero-mean corrections

    Q_i(k)= Σ_{S⊆{p|s}, |S|=i} Σ_{d|k/∏_{p∈S}p, d≤U} μ(d).

One can start directly from f₊B−f₋D_t and subtract log k·|f| Σ C_i Q_i. For exactly j small primes Q_j=1 and |Q_i|≤binom(j,i)2^{j−i}. The finite coefficient bound |B|,|D_t|≤2^j(2+1/t)log k follows from m≤1/t on this window. Choosing C_j=2^j(2+1/t)+1+Σ_{2≤i<j}C_i binom(j,i)2^{j−i} therefore makes every sector with 2≤j≤J nonpositive. Each probe has modulus ≤x^{(i+1)t}, finite tag multiplicity, zero harmonic Möbius mean with R_w, and at fixed polynomial input cost bounded in S_b units by O_{t,i}((1+log(t/e))^i [ρ(t/e)/e + E(t/(2e))/e²])+o_e(1). Consequently the construction can confine all still-adverse rank ≥3 contributions to inputs with more than J small factors, while carrying every earlier negative term in the complete equality.

These finite extensions transfer a growing debt. In particular when all input primes exceed U, the favorable f₊ composite row equals −f₊log k and survives every correction unchanged. Its total has magnitude ≫_f S_b/t for small fixed t in the successive large-x limits: the two-sided sieve with spare profile level gives ∑ f₊ R_U log k ∼_{t↓0} S₂e^{−γ}Σf₊/t, ∑f₊ is a positive multiple of S_b, and the genuine prime exception is O_f(S_b) by the complete prime upper on the positive angular profile. # Concentrating the complete signed upper on inputs with arbitrarily many small prime factors

Fix a positive integer $J$ and $0<t<1/[6(J+2)]$. Set $Y=x^t$, $H=x^{1/2-(J+2)t}$, and $L=\log x$. Write $k=n-2$ and use the dyadic interval, $S_b$, $S^\circ$, native signed outside $W(f)$, squarefree physical inputs, and $w=\exp(L^a)$ of *Removing the true semiprime inputs from the complete signed source*. Here $f=f_+-f_-$, both unsigned parts satisfying its bounded-rank profile progression estimate. The original sharp large coefficient and output cutoffs are preserved in $W(f)$.

For actual squarefree $k$ let $S=\{p\mid k:p\le Y\}$ and $m=\#\{p\mid k:Y<p\le H\}$. For any $T\subseteq S$ define
$$
 M(T)=\sum_{A\subseteq T,\,\prod A\le Y}(-1)^{|A|},\qquad
 h(T)=\sum_{p\in T}\log p .
$$
For $v=0,1$ write $D_v(T)=[(vm-1)\log k+h(T)]M(T)$. The quantities $m,k,Y$ remain the actual ones even when the argument of $D_v$ is a proper subset. For every $1\le|T|\le J$ set recursively
$$
 c_v(T)=-D_v(T)-
   \sum_{\varnothing\ne A\subsetneq T}c_v(A)M(T\setminus A).
\tag{1}
$$
Put
$$
 b_{v,J}(k)=1_{\mathbb P}(k)\log k+D_v(S)
   +\sum_{\varnothing\ne T\subseteq S,\,|T|\le J}
           c_v(T)M(S\setminus T).
\tag{2}
$$
For fixed $J,t$ we have
$$
 W(f)=\sum_{k+2\in I}R_w(k)\mu^2(k)
       [ f_+(k+2)b_{0,J}(k)-f_-(k+2)b_{1,J}(k)]+o_{J,t,f}(S_b).
\tag{3}
$$
For $z=x^\epsilon$ define $T_{>J,z}$ to be the right side of (3) restricted to $|S|>J$, with $R_w$ replaced by $R_z$ and the same squarefree restriction. For any $\eta>0$ one can choose $t$ and then $\epsilon\ll\min(t,\zeta)$, both fixed before the limit, so that
$$
 \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{W(f)-T_{>J,z}}{S_b}\le\eta .
\tag{4}
$$
Every input in $T_{>J,z}$ is squarefree, has at most $\lfloor1/\epsilon\rfloor$ prime factors, and at least $J+1$ of those lie in $(x^\epsilon,x^t]$. The two physical signs and all of their residual terms on this set are included.

## Primitive source accounting

Without the subset correction, (3) is the combination of the retuned base on $f_+$ and the single-marker retuned base on $f_-$. Both have exactly the same original prime-input term and primitive $-\mathfrak S_2\sum f_\pm$. The proof in the preceding paper also applies to this smaller $H$.

On inputs with $R_w(k)=1$ each selected prime in (1) exceeds $w$. The coefficient $c_v(T)$ depends only on the displayed factors of $T$, on $\log k$, and affinely on $m$. It is a sum of expressions $A(T)\log k+B(T)m\log k+E(T)$, where $|A|+|B|+|E|/L\le C_J$ with a finite constant depending on $J$ alone. For example an inductive majorant is $C_0=0$ and
$$
 C_j=3\cdot2^j+\sum_{i=1}^{j-1}\binom ji 2^{j-i} C_i.
$$
The term $h(T)\le L$ on every physical configuration and every grouped modulus below. Constants from this recursion can grow rapidly.

The complementary prefix $M(S\setminus T)$ expands into $e\mid k/\prod T$, $e\le Y$, with coefficient $\mu(e)$ and $(e,\prod T)=1$. On expanding the optional $m$, a label $Y<p\le H$ is distinct from all chosen small factors. A grouped modulus before the presieve is
$$
 d=e\prod_{r\in T}r\quad\text{or}\quad
 d=p e\prod_{r\in T}r\le H Y^{J+1}=x^{1/2-t}.
$$
The possible medium label is the unique factor of $d$ above $Y$; at most $O_J(L^J)$ identifications of $T$ share a modulus. Thus all errors of the bounded-rank primitive progression result fit with a fixed log loss at fixed $J$. Restoring subpower $R_w$ costs its usual arbitrarily accurate Bonferroni bracket, and the removal of rough nonsquarefree inputs uses Cauchy–Schwarz with the polynomial-in-$L$ multiplicity and $O(x/w)$ exceptions.

In the principal part the remaining Möbius sum $A_w(Y)$ excludes primes of $n$, $T$, and the optional $p$. The change in the full prefix caused by these exclusions is $O_J(L(1/w+x^{-\zeta}))$. The prime harmonic of each of the $J$ chosen factors costs $O(\log L)$, that of the optional medium factor is $O_t(1)$, and the logarithmic multiplier is at most $C_J L$. Consequently every added complete correction in (2) has mean $o_{J,t}(S_b)$ against either actual output profile. This proves (3). For ungrouped nonsquarefree majorants one can bound the number of choices of $T$ by $O_J(L^J)$ and the prefix terms by $\tau(k)$, which suffices with the same squareful deletion.

## The zero-small and nonempty strata

On true prime $k$ the medium and small sets are empty, so (2) gives zero from $\log k-\log k$. On composites with $1\le|S|\le J$, the last term with $T=S$ is $c_v(S)$, since $M(\varnothing)=1$. Recursion (1) cancels all displayed terms of (2) exactly. No intermediate sign bound is invoked.

On composite $S=\varnothing$, $b_{0,J}=-\log k$, hence $f_+b_{0,J}\le0$. For $\omega(k)\ge3$, $H^3>x$ ensures $m\ge1$, hence $-f_-b_{1,J}=-f_-(m-1)\log k\le0$. If $k=pq$ with $p<q$, $S=\varnothing$, and $p\le H$, its larger factor exceeds $H$ eventually and $m=1$. The negative channel is zero. Only $p>H$ can give positive mass there. The factor-product PNT, its level below one half and the upper sieve on $n=k+2$ prove that the normalized limsup of this last adverse mass is at most
$$
 \|f_-\|_\infty e^{-\gamma}F(\theta/\zeta)\zeta^{-1}
 \log\frac{1/2+(J+2)t}{1/2-(J+2)t},
$$
for fixed $\zeta<\theta<1/2$. This is $O_{f,J}(t)$. The complete zero-small pieces above are retained in the equality (3). Only the upper (4) can discard their favorable contributions.

## Polynomial input presieve

To transfer the added rows to $R_z$ use the fundamental lemma with auxiliary level $x^{t/2}$, as in the preceding paper. Every pre-sieve modulus is $\le x^{1/2-t}$. For each of the $J$ chosen variables between $z$ and $Y$ the additional absolute harmonic is $O(1+\log(t/\epsilon))$. The optional medium harmonic is at most $O_t(1)$. Their collective primitive per unit $S_b$ is
$$
 O_{J,t,f}\!\big((1+\log(t/\epsilon))^J
       [\epsilon^{-1}\rho(t/\epsilon)
                +\epsilon^{-2}E_{t/(2\epsilon)}]\big)+o_{J,t,\epsilon,f}(1).
$$
Here one uses the rough harmonic Möbius prefix $A_z(Y)=\rho(t/\epsilon)+o_\epsilon(1)$, the absolute $e$ harmonic $O(1/\epsilon)$, and $g_zL\ll1/\epsilon$. The factors removed by coprimality are now $>z$ or polynomial output primes, which cost $o_{J,t,\epsilon}(1)$ at fixed $\epsilon$. Marked-modulus coincidences are counted through the ungrouped absolute harmonic majorant in the main terms and through the $O_J(L^J)$ bound only for the progression discrepancies. No growing power of $L$ multiplies the fixed fundamental-lemma error. The retuned base also pays its Dickman tail as in the preceding paper. All these errors tend to zero at fixed $J,t$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$. For (4) first make the true semiprime cost less than $\eta/2$, then pay the presieve replacement with the remaining tolerance.

Constants, modulus headroom and prime thresholds depend on $J$. Inequality (4) alone gives no uniform integrability of its compensated high-order terms, no bound after taking $J\to\infty$ with the other cutoffs fixed, and no positive advantage on a genuine-prime class. The unknown quantity is the ordinary signed physical sum $T_{>J,z}$. Any uses at terminal scale must evaluate that sum or retain its full cost.

The distribution and sieve theorem numbers and primary references are in *Removing the true semiprime inputs from the complete signed source*. The subpower moment method in *The first small-factor strata of the compensated signed source* motivates the finite-subset expansion. Here its corrected sharp coefficients, polynomial moduli, two different output channels, and fixed-accuracy order of limits are explicit.
